Oklahoma State Department of Education tribal education guides (sde.ok.gov) now redirect to oklahoma.gov and could not be used; Minnesota Indian Affairs Council pages returned a captcha; North Dakota Indian Affairs Commission statistics page returned 403 (its 1998-era facts PDF was not used because it is outdated). Many figures are undated statements on current official pages: as_of is then the access date and confidence is medium. WebFetch-derived values come from a model summary of the page, so exact wording was requested and is quoted in notes, but they could not be checked against raw HTML. Language tags (ISO 639-3) were assigned by the researcher from the language named on the source; where the source names only a people or a broad group, no language fact was recorded. Self-designations were recorded only where the source presents the term as the people's own name; band-level or ancestral terms are flagged in notes. Several nations publish conflicting figures on different pages (Northfork, Tesuque, Tunica-Biloxi, Tejon, Ysleta del Sur, Santo Domingo, NHBP, Salt River); conflicts are described in notes. Website facts were recorded only for Passamaquoddy (none in BIA directory) and San Carlos Apache (BIA lists an intertribal-council page). Email-general recorded only for Turtle Mountain and Zuni.
log.narrative: Read the contract, selected the 201 roster entries (list contiguous-48, official_name M-Z). Crawled each nation's directory website (home page plus key About/History/Enrollment/Language pages), extracted candidate sentences with regular expressions (numbers near enrolled/members/citizens/population; sentences naming languages or self-names), and reviewed them by hand. Recorded facts only where the page states them; each fact's URL was re-verified automatically against the fetched page text (exceptions are sums or numbers written in words, noted). A second, deeper crawl covered nations still lacking population. For blocked sites I used WebFetch. For large or unpublished nations I used targeted web searches that surfaced official news releases/PDFs (Navajo, Chickasaw, Pascua Yaqui, Mescalero, Omaha) and state-agency tribal profiles (South Dakota Tribal Relations, Wisconsin DPI, Minnesota DOT, North Dakota Indian Affairs Commission, Maine DOE) plus Inter Tribal Council of Arizona pages, at medium confidence. Wikipedia was not used as a source. Small California rancherias and many Washington and New Mexico nations do not publish enrollment counts on their sites.
